Board, MLK, Civil Rights Acts 1964/65), Vietnam War, Watergate, Reagan conservatism, 9/11 2001, War on Terror (Afghanistan/Iraq), 2008 financial crisis, Obama first Black president, Trump populism, January 6 2021 Capitol attack, Biden, and global hegemony.

religion.note: Christian majority declining; evangelical Protestantism politically powerful; Catholic (largest denomination, Irish/Italian/Hispanic immigration); Jewish (~6M, influential); Muslim growing (~3.5M); Hindu (Indian immigration); no religion fastest-growing (Gen Z); separation church/state (First Amendment); Bible Belt (South); religious right (Reagan coalition); megachurches; Mormons (Utah); denominational diversity

ethnic_groups.name: Non-Hispanic White
ethnic_groups.notes: European descent (British, German, Irish, Italian, Polish, etc.); majority declining; WASPs (White Anglo-Saxon Protestants) historically dominant; Ellis Island immigration 1890-1920s; ethnic melting pot ideology; 'white' category expanded over time (Irish/Italians/Jews became white)

ethnic_groups.name: Hispanic/Latino
ethnic_groups.notes: Mexican (largest, 60%+), Puerto Rican, Cuban, Central American, South American; Spanish-speaking; Catholic/evangelical; fastest-growing; Southwest historically Mexican territory (annexed 1848); immigration debates; diverse (white/mestizo/indigenous/Afro-Latino); politically divided (Cuban conservatives, Mexican progressives)

ethnic_groups.name: Black/African American
ethnic_groups.notes: Descendants of enslaved Africans (1619-1865, ~4M enslaved by 1860); Civil War/Emancipation 1865; Reconstruction/Jim Crow; Great Migration (South to North, 1916-70, 6M); Civil Rights Movement (1954-68, MLK, desegregation); Black Lives Matter; systemic racism legacy; culturally foundational (jazz, hip-hop, etc.); politically Democratic; disparities (incarceration, wealth gap)

ethnic_groups.name: Asian American
ethnic_groups.notes: Chinese (Exclusion Act 1882, railroad workers), Indian (IT/medical, largest immigrant group), Filipino, Vietnamese (refugees 1975), Korean, Japanese (internment WWII); model minority myth; diverse; politically moderate; significant California presence

ethnic_groups.name: Native American/Alaska Native
ethnic_groups.notes: Indigenous peoples (~6.9M including mixed); Trail of Tears, Indian Wars, reservations, boarding schools ('kill the Indian, save the man'), genocide; ~574 federally recognized tribes; sovereignty issues; cultural revival; casino gaming; Wounded Knee; activists (AIM, Dakota Access Pipeline); diverse nations (Navajo largest, Cherokee, Choctaw, Sioux, Apache, etc.)

ethnic_groups.name: Native Hawaiian/Pacific Islander
ethnic_groups.notes: Hawaiian, Samoan, Guamanian, etc.; annexed Hawaii 1898 (overthrew kingdom); small but distinct

ethnic_groups.name: Two or more races

country_profile.time_zone: Multiple (UTC-5 to UTC-10: EST, CST, MST, PST, AKST, HST)
country_profile.notes_unique: Global superpower; world's largest economy ($28.8T); reserve currency (US dollar); most powerful military (11 aircraft carriers, 750+ foreign bases); nuclear arsenal; NATO leader; UN P5 member; Marshall Plan rebuilt Europe post-WWII; Cold War victor 1991; liberal international order architect; cultural hegemony (Hollywood, Silicon Valley, Coca-Cola, McDonald's); immigration nation ('melting pot', 'nation of immigrants', Statue of Liberty); moon landing 1969; 50 states + DC; slavery legacy (12.5M Africans enslaved, 1619-1865, only resolved by Civil War with 750,000 dead); westward expansion/genocide of indigenous ('Manifest Destiny'); atomic bomb 1945 (Hiroshima/Nagasaki, only nation to use in war); longest Constitution (1787, world's oldest codified); separation of powers; Electoral College; two-party system (Democrat/Republican); gun culture (Second Amendment, 400M+ guns); mass incarceration (2M+ imprisoned, highest rate); healthcare inequalities; income inequality (top 1%); climate change ambivalence; exceptionalism ideology; Hollywood; jazz/blues/rock/hip-hop; national parks; Grand Canyon; Silicon Valley (tech giants: Apple, Google, Microsoft, Meta); Space exploration (NASA); 9/11 attacks 2001 (2,977 dead, War on Terror); January 6, 2021 (Capitol attack, Trump); Trump 2024 comeback (47th president, first since Grover Cleveland non-consecutive terms)

comparative_rankings._note: Country position relative to continent and global. 'rank' = 1 is best/largest.

current_leader.name: Donald Trump
current_leader.title: President
current_leader.notes: 47th president; Republican; real estate businessman/TV personality; populist nationalist; 'America First'; defeated Harris 2024; first president since Cleveland with non-consecutive terms; first president with felony conviction (34 counts); twice impeached (Ukraine, January 6); January 6, 2021 Capitol attack; tariffs/trade wars; immigration hardliner; polarizing; oldest president

former_leaders.name: Joe Biden
former_leaders.notes: 46th; Democrat; oldest president (inaugurated 78); defeated Trump 2020; VP under Obama; withdrew 2024 race (oldest nominee concern); infrastructure/climate bills; COVID response; Ukraine aid; inflation; pardoned son Hunter

former_leaders.name: Donald Trump
former_leaders.notes: 45th; first president with no prior government/military experience; defeated Clinton 2016 (lost popular vote, Electoral College); tax cuts; deregulation; 3 SCOTUS justices; Muslim ban; family separation (border); denied COVID severity; lost 2020; refused concession; January 6, 2021 Capitol attack; second impeachment; indicted 4 cases (91 felony counts); convicted NYC (34 counts); returned 2025

former_leaders.name: Barack Obama
former_leaders.notes: 44th; first Black president; Democrat; Harvard Law; Affordable Care Act (Obamacare); killed Bin Laden 2011; Iran nuclear deal; same-sex marriage legalized; Deferred Action (DACA); Nobel Peace Prize 2009; good economy recovery; polarized opposition (birtherism/Trump); 'Yes We Can'; historic

former_leaders.name: George W. Bush
former_leaders.notes: 43rd; Republican; son of 41st; lost popular vote 2000 (Bush v. Gore); 9/11 attacks; War on Terror; invaded Afghanistan 2001; Iraq War 2003 (WMDs false); Patriot Act; Hurricane Katrina; 2008 financial crisis; unpopular exit; rehabilitated image

former_leaders.name: Bill Clinton
former_leaders.notes: 42nd; Democrat; youngest elected (46); Arkansas governor; economy boomed (tech bubble); NAFTA; welfare reform; balanced budget; Monica Lewinsky scandal; impeached 1998 (perjury/obstruction, acquitted); survived; popular exit

former_leaders.name: George H. W. Bush
former_leaders.notes: 41st; Republican; VP under Reagan; Gulf War 1991 (liberated Kuwait); Cold War ended (USSR collapsed 1991, 'won' Cold War); 'New World Order'; broke tax pledge ('Read my lips'); lost 1992 (recession); patrician WASP; CIA director

former_leaders.name: Ronald Reagan
former_leaders.notes: 40th; Republican; actor; conservative revolution; Reaganomics (tax cuts, deregulation, trickle-down); 'government is the problem'; Cold War escalation ('Evil Empire', arms race, SDI); Gorbachev ('tear down this wall', Berlin Wall fell 1989); Iran-Contra scandal; assassination attempt 1981; oldest president (until Trump/Biden); Alzheimer's

former_leaders.name: Jimmy Carter
former_leaders.notes: 39th; Democrat; peanut farmer/Georgia governor; human rights focus; Camp David Accords 1978 (Egypt-Israel); Iran hostage crisis 1979-81 (444 days, defined presidency); energy crisis; stagflation; lost badly 1980; post-presidency humanitarian (Nobel Peace 2002); lived to 100 (died 2024)

former_leaders.name: Richard Nixon
former_leaders.notes: 37th; Republican; VP under Eisenhower; opened China 1972 (Mao meeting); ended Vietnam draft; Watergate scandal (break-in, cover-up); resigned August 1974 (only president to resign, facing impeachment); pardoned by Ford; 'Tricky Dick'

former_leaders.name: Abraham Lincoln
former_leaders.notes: 16th; Republican (first GOP president); Civil War (1861-65, preserved Union); Emancipation Proclamation 1863 (freed slaves); 13th Amendment (abolished slavery); assassinated April 14, 1865 (John Wilkes Booth, Ford's Theatre); greatest president (historians); martyr

former_leaders.name: George Washington
former_leaders.notes: 1st; Federalist; Revolutionary War commander; Constitutional Convention; set precedents (two terms, peaceful transfer); 'Father of His Country'; Farewell Address (warned against parties/foreign entanglements); slaveholder; Mount Vernon
